_note: Narrative events, delivered as letters. phase: march | winter. Placeholders: {captain} {employer} {enemy} {town}. See sim/event_engine.gd for condition and effect keys.

events.title: Ambush at the ford
events.text: Scouts report enemy crossbowmen in the reeds by the ford ahead of {town}.

outcomes.text: You fight your way across.

choices.text: Take the long road around (lose time).

outcomes.text: The detour costs forage and patience.

choices.text: Send the light horse to flush them out.

outcomes.text: The stradiots scatter them and take a few prisoners.
The stradiots ride into a hail of bolts.

events.title: Fever in the camp
events.text: A camp fever spreads through the tents. The physicians want money; the priests want prayers.

outcomes.text: The fever breaks.
Physicians are expensive and useless.

choices.text: March on and trust in God.

outcomes.text: The fever takes its toll.

events.title: A merchant convoy
events.text: A Florentine merchant convoy passes your column, lightly guarded and heavily laden.

choices.text: Offer to escort it for a fee.

outcomes.text: The merchants pay for your protection.
Your men eat well tonight. Florence will hear of it.
The convoy rolls on.

events.title: A challenge
events.text: An enemy condottiere sends a herald: he challenges {captain} to single combat before the armies.

choices.text: Accept for the honour of the company.

outcomes.text: {captain} unhorses him. Songs will be sung.
{captain} is carried from the field, badly wounded.

choices.text: Refuse. Wars are won by armies.

outcomes.text: Some of the men mutter about cowardice.

events.title: Deserters seek service
events.text: Sixty footmen who walked away from their unpaid captain ask to join your company.

choices.text: Take them on as a band of sword-and-buckler men.

outcomes.text: A new band joins, green but eager.

choices.text: Men who desert once desert twice. Send them away.

outcomes.text: They leave, cursing.

events.title: Heavy rain
events.text: Days of rain turn the roads to mud. Powder and bowstrings will suffer if you fight now.

outcomes.text: The next battle will be fought in the wet.

choices.text: Wait for the weather to clear (costs forage).

outcomes.text: The sun returns, eventually.

events.title: The proveditore asks questions
events.text: The {employer} proveditore riding with your company asks why your scouts met enemy riders under a flag of truce.

choices.text: Explain it was a prisoner exchange.

outcomes.text: He writes it down, and seems satisfied.
He writes it down, and does not seem satisfied.
His report will be glowing.
He takes the money and reports the bribe.

events.title: Remember Carmagnola
events.text: An old friend writes: 'Venice invited Carmagnola to dine at the Doge's palace in 1432. They beheaded him between the columns. Do not give them cause.'

outcomes.text: You watch it curl in the fire.

choices.text: Send a gift to the Council of Ten (300 florins).

outcomes.text: The Ten acknowledge your gift.

events.title: The village of San Pietro
events.text: Your column camps near a prosperous village. The headman offers a small purse to be left alone.

choices.text: Take the purse and move on.

outcomes.text: Honest extortion.

choices.text: Take the purse and the village.

outcomes.text: The men are pleased. The chroniclers are not.

choices.text: Refuse the purse. Pay for your forage.

outcomes.text: Word spreads of a company that pays its way.

events.title: A German gunsmith
events.text: A Nuremberg gunsmith offers to train a band of your men in the handgun, years before it is common in Italy.

outcomes.text: Handgunners can now be recruited.
He heads for Milan instead.

events.title: Bad blood
events.text: {captain} and another of your captains came to blows over a woman, a horse, or a debt. Accounts differ.

outcomes.text: {captain} is grateful. The other is not.

choices.text: Fine them both (and keep the money).

outcomes.text: Neither is happy, but the camp is quiet.
Money heals most wounds.

events.title: A lean winter
events.text: Grain is dear in {town} this winter. The quartermaster needs more money or the men go hungry.

outcomes.text: Bellies full.
The men grumble, and some slip away.

events.title: Poison in the wine
events.text: A servant is caught with a vial of something that is not wine. Your enemies are many.

choices.text: Hang him and double the guard.

outcomes.text: You sleep with a dagger under your pillow.
The second assassin was already inside.
He names a former employer. Useful.
He names nobody and dies.

events.title: An old soldier
events.text: A grey-bearded captain who served under Braccio da Montone asks for a place in your company.

choices.text: Take him on (150 florins signing gift).

outcomes.text: A new captain joins the company.
He wishes you luck.

events.title: A letter from Francesco Sforza
events.text: The great condottiere writes to you as one professional to another: 'Our employers think they own us. They rent us.'

outcomes.text: A useful friendship.

choices.text: Forward it to your employer as proof of loyalty.

outcomes.text: Your employer is impressed. Sforza is not.

events.title: The men want their pay
events.text: A delegation of sergeants stands in your doorway. They have not been paid, and they have pikes.

outcomes.text: They believe you. For now.
They do not believe you.
You eat off pewter this winter.

events.title: An indulgence
events.text: A friar offers the company a papal indulgence for its sins, for a price.

outcomes.text: Your sins are lighter; so is your purse.
The friar moves on.

events.title: The horse fair at {town}
events.text: A horse fair offers remounts at good prices.

outcomes.text: Your lances are well horsed.
